parole.testo: Internationalism; compare English agglomerate. Possibly borrowed from French agglomérat or from German Agglomerat, ultimately from Latin agglomerō + -at. First attested in 1833.

parole.significato: academic, member of an academy (member of an institution or building for the study of higher learning)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Latin acadēmicus. Etymology 2 sense 2, etymology 2 sense 4 and etymology 2 sense 5 are semantic loans from German Akademiker and French académicien. First attested in 1577.

parole.significato: action, mission, campaign, operation (something done in order to accomplish something)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Latin āctiō (“act of doing or making”). Noun sense 1 and noun sense 6 are semantic loans from German Aktion or French action. First attested in 1553.
Learned borrowing from Latin āctus. Etymology 1 sense 5 is a semantic loan from German Akt. First attested in 1529.

parole.significato: album (book specially designed to keep photographs, stamps, or autographs)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Album or French album. First attested in 1609.

parole.significato: anatomy (science that deals with the form and structure of organic bodies)
parole.testo: Internationalism; possibly borrowed from German Anatomie, or French anatomie, ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀνατομή (anatomḗ, “dissection”). By surface analysis, ana- + -tomia. First attested in the 16th century.

parole.significato: fingering (a specific method of using the fingers to play an instrument)
parole.testo: From either German Apllikatur or Italian applicatura.
Either borrowed from French attentat or borrowed from German Attentat.

parole.significato: attraction (event, location, or business that has a tendency to draw interest from visitors, and in many cases, local r…
parole.testo: Either borrowed from French attraction or German Attraktion, from Old French attraction, from Latin attractiō.

parole.significato: current (existing or occurring at the moment)
parole.testo: From bieżeć + -ący. Adjective sense 1 is a semantic loan from German laufend, French courant, and English current. First attested in 1500–1547.

parole.significato: bitch (inmate used as a sexual object)
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from German Schwelle or from German schwul.

parole.significato: director (person in charge of a directorate)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Latin dīrēctor. Noun 1 sense 1 and noun 1 sense 2 are semantic loans from German Direktor and French directeur.

parole.significato: operation (activity undertaken by someone for a specific purpose)
parole.testo: From działalny + -ość. Sense 1 is a semantic loan from German Tätigkeit and French activité. First attested in 1802.

parole.significato: improvisation (the act or art of composing and making music, poetry, and the like, extemporaneously)
parole.testo: From either German Improvisation or French improvisation, from Italian improvvisazione.
From either Russian казарма (kazarma) or German Kaserne, ultimately from Italian caserma.

parole.significato: landscape (portion of territory which the eye can comprehend in a single view)
parole.testo: From kraj + obraz. Calque of German Landschaft or French paysage. Coined by Joachim Lelewel.

parole.significato: king (male monarch; a man who heads a monarchy)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish król. Noun 2 sense 2, noun 2 sense 3, and noun 2 sense 4 and are an internationalism semantic loan; compare English king, French roi and German König. Doublet of Karol.

parole.significato: minute (unit of time equal to sixty seconds)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish minuta. Sense 1 is a semantic loan from French minute or German Minute. Doublet of menu.

parole.significato: international (of or having to do with more than one nation)
parole.testo: From między- + narodowy. Internationalism calque of various European languages; compare English international, French international, German international. First attested in 1859. parole.significato: hand puppet, glove puppet (type of puppet designed to be worn on the hand like a glove)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps borrowed from German Patsche + -yna + -ka. Alternatively, from earlier *palcynka, from palec (“finger”). Etymology 1 sense 3 is a semantic loan from English sock puppet.

parole.significato: plan (a set of intended actions, usually mutually related, through which one expects to achieve a goal)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French plan. Sense 1 is a semantic loan from English plan and German Plan. First attested in the 19th century.

parole.significato: train (mechanical (traditionally steam-powered, now typically diesel or electrical) vehicle carrying a large number of…
parole.testo: Deverbal from pociągać. Sense 1 is a semantic loan from French train, English train, and German Zug. Sense 2 is a semantic loan from French inclination. First attested in 1550.

parole.significato: design (plan for the structure and functions of an artifact, building or system)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Projekt. First attested in 1656–1688. Sense 5 is a semantic loan from English project.

parole.significato: representative (one who represents someone or something)
parole.testo: From przedstawić + -ciel. Calque of French représentant or German Vertreter. First attested in 1820. Compare Czech představitel and Russian представи́тель (predstavítelʹ).

parole.significato: rightness, righteousness; fairness (that what is right, fair, or in accordance with reality)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Latin ratiō. Noun sense 6 is a semantic loan from German Ration. First attested in 1548. Doublet of rezon (“self-confidence”). Compare Silesian racyjŏ.

parole.significato: sewer, street gutter (prepared channel in a surface)
